$comment: M-029 · The India ten-document KYC checklist — LAUNCH_MARKET_INDIA.md §6, SeedStrategy.md §3.5.
FOUR CHECKLISTS, ONE PER entity_type_enum VALUE. SeedStrategy.md §3.5: 'seeded as four rows —
one per entity_type_enum value — because the required documents differ by entity type'. The
difference is real and narrow: only BUSINESS_REGISTRATION's accepted documents change. The other
nine items are identical, and they are written out per checklist rather than inherited, because a
reviewer checking this file against §6 must be able to read one checklist top to bottom.
IDEMPOTENT (P11). The natural key is (countryCode, entityType, version). Re-applying this file
changes nothing; publishing an edit means writing kyc_checklists.in.v2.json and superseding v1,
never editing this file — an application that snapshotted v1 must keep reading the v1 it was
actually judged against (ERD.md §9.6).
NO THRESHOLD IS STATED ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
Gym.md O-TEN-4 records the GSTIN registration threshold as a tax fact awaiting an Indian tax
advisor, and says §10.1 'states the structure and refuses to state the threshold'.
LAUNCH_MARKET_INDIA.md §13 says the same of every rate and threshold in it. So the conditional
items key off facts the APPLICANT declares — their GST registration status, whether their
municipality requires a trade licence — rather than off a number this repository would be
inventing. A wrong threshold in seed data is a wrong checklist shown to every gym in India, and
it would look exactly like a right one.
Exactly two operators. Kept this small on purpose: a condition language is a program, and a
program in reference data is one nobody reviews. resolve-checklist.use-case.ts refuses any
operator not named here rather than ignoring it — an unknown operator that silently evaluated
false would drop a required document from the checklist without a word.
$conditionVocabulary.taxRegistrationStatusIn: true when tenants.tax_registration_status is one of the listed values
$conditionVocabulary.declaredByApplicant: true when the applicant answered yes to the named declaration. Used where the fact is legal or municipal and the platform cannot know it

items.label: PAN card
items.helpText: The proprietor's own PAN. A sole proprietorship has no PAN of its own — it trades on the proprietor's personal PAN, so the fourth character is P.

items.label: GST registration certificate
items.helpText: Required if you are registered for GST. The GSTIN embeds your state code and your PAN, and both must match what you have entered.

items.label: Udyam / MSME registration certificate
items.helpText: Proof that the business legally exists.

items.label: Shop & Establishment registration
items.helpText: Issued by your municipality and specific to your state.

items.label: Bank account proof
items.helpText: A cancelled cheque or a bank statement showing the account name. Payouts go to this account and nowhere else.
acceptedDocuments: Bank statement showing the account name

items.label: Owner identity document
items.helpText: One government photo ID for the person behind the business, in addition to PAN.
items.$comment: AADHAAR IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. LAUNCH_MARKET_INDIA.md §6 and §13.6: Aadhaar carries statutory handling restrictions, so the platform asks for PAN plus a non-Aadhaar ID and avoids those obligations entirely. Adding it is a successor version after legal sign-off, never an edit to this file.

items.label: Address proof for the premises
items.helpText: A utility bill or rent agreement for the gym address. It is checked against the pin you place on the map.

items.label: Municipal trade licence
items.helpText: Required in some cities and not others. Tell us whether yours requires one.

items.label: Fire safety NOC
items.helpText: Commonly required above a floor-area threshold set by your state. Tell us whether your premises is above it.

items.label: Music licence (PPL / IPRS)
items.helpText: Playing recorded music in a commercial space generally needs a copyright licence. We flag this for you — it does not hold up your approval.

$comment: Trusts, societies, HUFs and section-8 companies all arrive here, because entity_type_enum
has four values and Indian entity law has more. BUSINESS_REGISTRATION therefore lists
several accepted documents rather than naming one — the reviewer reads which was supplied.
This is NOT a lighter checklist: every other item is identical to the other three, and
pan.vo.ts refuses OTHER just as strictly, accepting only the entity characters that
genuinely belong to these forms.
